headline: Reshape consecutive blocks without reordering
statement: Construct a matrix with m rows and n columns using every entry of original in row-major order. Return an empty list if the requested shape has a different number of cells.
intuition: A matrix with m rows and n columns needs exactly m × n values. Check that size first. Then take consecutive groups of n input values as rows. The groups preserve the original order and use each value exactly once; no rearrangement is required.
approach: For each row index, compute its starting offset.
Copy the next n elements into a new row.
correctness: The size check ensures the required cells equal the available entries. The row blocks are consecutive, disjoint, and cover offsets zero through m*n-1 exactly once. Therefore every value appears in its original order in the required matrix shape.
bruteForce: Assign each value individually using row=index//n and col=index%n. This has the same linear complexity; slicing emphasizes the consecutive row blocks.

complexity.time: O(mn) for a valid shape; O(1) if invalid
complexity.explanation: Each original entry is copied into exactly one output row.

pitfalls: Do not transpose the row-major order.
Reject both too few and too many entries.
Create distinct row lists rather than repeating one mutable row.
